items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: I was with Warren Covington on a schlock rock & roll date at a horrible studio back in the 60s.

ctx.x: I was with Warren Covington on a schlock rock & roll date at a horrible studio back in the 60s. And there was a black singer, a lady, and the studio was kind of dirty, funky is a better word, dirty. And she was singing a song called “The Ghoul in School” which went “I was lying in my bed/in my school out of town/when all of a sudden/I heard a horrible sound.” And then you have [scats/sings] “it was the ghoul, in school.” As bad as it can

get. It was just rotten, absolutely rotten, retched. Now she sang this. We played it. Now it’s break time. You have to know Warren Covington. Warren Covington was a wonderful trombone player, had his own band and he was like Mr. Indiana, with the sweater, always looked nice, always had his face washed and hands and nails manicured and the whole thing, he was just as collegiate as he could be you know. And about twelve years older than me I guess. We were the only two trombones. We’re sitting there. And now the…
